children: Basis bids for corn shipped by barge to the US Gulf Coast firmed on Tuesday as the Midwest harvest entered its final stages, but export premiums declined, traders said.
A slide in Chicago Board of Trade corn futures (CZ26) to four-month lows curbed farmer grain sales, and CBOT soybean futures (SF27) hit a 2-1/2 month low on expectations of large US harvests.

After the close of CBOT trading, brokerage StoneX raised its estimate of the average US 2026 corn yield to 183.1 bushels per acre (bpa) from 182.1 last month, and upped its soybean yield forecast to 55.0 bpa, from 54.1 previously.

The US Department of Agriculture confirmed private sales of 315,000 metric tons of US corn to Mexico and another 136,000 tons to South Korea, along with sales of 134,000 tons of  soybeans to undisclosed destinations.
At the Gulf, CIF corn barges loaded in November were bid at 94 cents over CBOT December corn (CZ26) futures, up 2 cents from Monday.

But FOB export premiums for Gulf corn vessels loaded in late November were around 106 cents over December futures, down 3 cents, and December premiums were around 110 cents over futures, down a penny.
For soybeans, CIF barges loaded in November were bid at 115 cents over CBOT November soybean (SX26) futures, unchanged from Monday.
Traders were starting to roll soybean bids to the CBOT January soybean futures contract (SF27) as the November contract (SX26) nears its expiration next week.
November-loaded soy barges traded at 106 cents over CBOT January (SF27) futures, or the equivalent of 117 cents over November futures, given the 11-cent difference between the two futures contracts.
FOB export premiums for Gulf soybeans loaded in December, the first month available, were steady at about 118 cents over CBOT January futures.
